text:
dylan: Heads-up 0: Acero adapter looks good functionally but int4 run shows big format regressions and hallucination spikes on their structured-response QA set.
mira: can you paste a failing example?
dylan: example: 
```\nInput: 'Extract invoice details and return JSON {amount, currency, due_date}'\nExpected: `{\"amount\": 123.45, \"currency\": \"USD\", \"due_date\": \"2026-03-20\"}`\nGot: 'Looks like the invoice was for a hundred and twenty bucks due soon. You should check the platform.'\n```\noscar: yikes. That looks like the model is dropping the schema constraint entirely after int4 quant. Did you run fp16 baseline?
dylan: fp16 is fine. int8 minor noise but still returns JSON shape; int4 returns prose ~12% of the time, compared to 0.6% baseline. Hallucination rate up ~+11% on devset.
jen: maybe activation dynamic range mismatch after folding LN for int4? We saw similar in beta-quant experiments. Do we have per-layer calibration enabled?
mira: the standard pipeline was `quantize --scheme awq --bits 4 --calibrate global` for this run. No per-layer.
oscar: try `--calibrate per_layer --calib-steps 2048` and enable `--preserve-schema-constraints` in eval harness if available. Also run `--seed 42` to reproduce.
dylan: launching calibration sweep now. Command: `./eval_harness --model base_v2.0+acero-adapter --quant int4 --calibrate per_layer --calib-steps 2048 --batch 8 --timeout 1800 --preserve-schema-constraints true`
ci-bot: job 11012 started on quant-sim-3. ETA 18m
merge-bot: noted: Acero adapter merged on main (commit a9f3b2). Upload artifact: s3://redwood-evals/acero/onboard-2026-03-21.tar.gz
dylan: quick initial results: int4+per_layer calibration reduced prose outputs to 3.2%, hallucination delta +2.1%. Still worse than int8 but far better than previous.
jen: progress. That indicates calibration was masking some layer-level scale collapse. But we still have schema failures (~9% of cases). Could be tokenization or prompt encoding differences for structured tasks.
oscar: check the prompt wrappers in adapter training; did they use `response_format: text` vs `response_format: json`? If adapter was trained with lax prompts that encourage prose, quantization exaggerates that.
mira: training config shows `response_format: json_strict` — so adapter should obey. Hmm.
dylan: plan: 1) hold routing to prefer int8 for Acero customer while we iterate (I'll open PR), 2) add per-layer calibration to onboarding quant pipeline by default, 3) add a schema-consistency check in the quick eval pack that rejects int4 if JSON-schema pass rate < 95%, 4) add an Optimize rule warning when adapter training uses ambiguous response prompts.
jen: also add a small synthetic stress test that injects edge-case tokens (unicode, long numerics) into the devset to catch tokenizer/serialization breakage.
oscar: agree. I'll prototype a lightweight `schema-smoke` harness in ml/tools/evals and add unit tests. ETA EOD.
dylan: opened PR 8399 to prefer int8 routing for Acero until validation passes. PTAL.
ci-bot: PR 8399 tests passed in CI, canary deploy queued.
merge-bot: Canary deploy succeeded for routing change (stage.acero -> prefer int8).
mira: follow-ups: 1) persist eval artifacts to experiments store with tags `acero,onboard,int4-calib`, 2) add onboarding checklist item `run-schema-smoke + per-layer calibration`, 3) update docs for recommended quant params for structured-output adapters.
dylan: added tasks to ticket ENGML-2178 and assigned owners. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
jen: one more ask 0: add Optimize suggestion to flag adapters that used free-text prompts in training if they are intended for structured outputs. That should prevent noisy merges.
oscar: will do. Creating lightweight detector that scans training prompts for schema tokens and gives a confidence score.
dylan: nice work team, re-run full QA after oscar's harness is in and then we'll consider unblocking int4 for Acero. :rocket:
